text: Our platform vendor already does this. Fear of tool sprawl and of explaining another line item. Compare what the bundled feature covers today against the sources and depth this problem needs, then decide whether the gap is worth a separate tool.

title: It's not in this year's budget.
text: It's not in this year's budget. No clear owner for the spend, or the problem hasn't been tied to a risk the board tracks. Find whose existing budget this replaces or protects, and tie the problem to an exposure already on the risk register.

title: You haven't passed our security review yet.
text: You haven't passed our security review yet. Procurement or legal needs paperwork before anyone will sign. Send the security pack, DPA, and data-flow summary early so the review runs in parallel with evaluation.

title: We need multi-year terms for that price.
text: We need multi-year terms for that price. Procurement wants a discount and fewer renewals. Trade term length for price protection and an exit tied to agreed success measures.

title: Does vendor onboarding include a security review step?
text: Does vendor onboarding include a security review step? Security questionnaires before contract.

title: Is there a renewal date for an overlapping tool?
text: Is there a renewal date for an overlapping tool? A contract end date within a year.

title: Is the company in a buying freeze?
text: Is the company in a buying freeze? A freeze on new vendors.

text: Legal / general counsel Approve contract and data terms; judge incident disclosure obligations. ic: Legal Counsel, Commercial Legal Counsel senior-ic: Senior Legal Counsel, Lead Legal Counsel manager: Legal Manager, Commercial Legal Manager director: Director of Legal, Head of Legal vp: VP of Legal

title: You haven't passed our security review yet.

title: We can't give a vendor access to that data.
text: We can't give a vendor access to that data. Privacy, residency, or contract limits on sharing code or customer data. Clarify what leaves the environment, what is stored, and whether a self-hosted or scoped option exists.

title: Legal and HR won't let us monitor employees that closely.
text: Legal and HR won't let us monitor employees that closely. Privacy, labor law, and trust concerns. Bring legal and HR in early, scope monitoring to risk signals, and agree on who sees what.

title: Will legal review data processing terms for this purchase?
text: Will legal review data processing terms for this purchase? A DPA or data-processing review in the process.

title: Is there regulatory disclosure exposure (SEC, NYDFS, DORA)?
text: Is there regulatory disclosure exposure (SEC, NYDFS, DORA)? Rules that require reporting or certification.

title: Has legal blocked similar tools before?
text: Has legal blocked similar tools before? Past refusals on data access.

title: Board / audit or risk committee
text: Board / audit or risk committee Oversee cyber risk; hold management accountable. c-level: Board, Audit committee, Risk committee, Board of directors

title: Personal accountability for cyber oversight in regulated sectors
text: Personal accountability for cyber oversight in regulated sectors

title: Hard to judge security posture from management reports
text: Hard to judge security posture from management reports

title: The board needs a simple answer, not more detail.
text: The board needs a simple answer, not more detail. Directors can't judge technical reports. Offer one or two measures the board can track over time, tied to risks already on the register.

title: Does the board review cyber risk at least quarterly?
text: Does the board review cyber risk at least quarterly? A standing cyber agenda item.

title: Is the company public or heavily regulated?
text: Is the company public or heavily regulated? SEC, NYDFS, DORA or sector oversight.

title: Does the board have no cyber oversight assigned?
text: Does the board have no cyber oversight assigned? No committee owns cyber.

title: Offboarding has no clear owner, so former staff keep access

title: Access changes lag HR events
text: Access changes lag HR events

title: People-risk cases need fairness and privacy
text: People-risk cases need fairness and privacy

title: Legal and HR won't let us monitor employees that closely.
text: Legal and HR won't let us monitor employees that closely. Privacy, labor law, and trust concerns. Bring legal and HR in early, scope monitoring to risk signals, and agree on who sees what.

title: HR data isn't clean enough to drive access.
text: HR data isn't clean enough to drive access. Joiner, mover and leaver events in HR are late or wrong. Start with leavers and contractors, where late changes create the most risk.

title: Does access removal lag HR terminations?
text: Does access removal lag HR terminations? Former employees with active accounts.

title: Is HR involved in insider risk or awareness programs?
text: Is HR involved in insider risk or awareness programs? HR on the insider risk group.

title: Is HR data unreliable or spread across systems?
text: Is HR data unreliable or spread across systems? No single HR system of record.

title: Workforce identity
text: Workforce identity The directory, identity provider, single sign-on, MFA or passwordless, and provisioning path employees and contractors use to get into company systems. How does a person prove who they are, and how does that account get created and removed?

title: Directory plus per-app local accounts
text: Directory plus per-app local accounts A handful of SaaS apps and one office directory. Dozens of apps, contractors, and MFA or offboarding gaps an auditor or insurer asks about.

title: Identity features bundled in the productivity suite
text: Identity features bundled in the productivity suite Most apps already sign in through the suite and policies are simple. Conditional access, non-suite apps, or lifecycle automation become requirements.

title: Customer identity (CIAM)
text: Customer identity (CIAM) Authentication and account experience for customers, partners, or developers using your product. This is a different buyer and budget from workforce IGA. How do customers or developers sign up, sign in, and consent without becoming an employee identity?

title: Homegrown login and user store
text: Homegrown login and user store An early product with one sign-in flow and a small user base. Social login, B2B tenants, MFA, fraud, or regional data rules pile onto the team.

title: Open-source auth library or self-hosted identity server
text: Open-source auth library or self-hosted identity server A strong platform team that wants control and can run it. Uptime, upgrades, and compliance evidence for the identity service become a full-time job.

title: Identity governance (IGA)
text: Identity governance (IGA) Joiner-mover-leaver, access requests, certifications, role mining, separation of duties, audit evidence, and remediation. IGA decides who should have access and whether they still should. Who should have this access, who approved it, and can we prove that at audit time?

title: Ticket-based access requests and spreadsheet reviews
text: Ticket-based access requests and spreadsheet reviews Few apps and a light audit scope. Audit findings on reviews, slow joiner/mover/leaver, or SOX scope grows.

title: Identity provider lifecycle features
text: Identity provider lifecycle features Most apps are SSO-connected and roles are simple. Separation of duties, certifications, and non-SSO apps are in scope.

title: PAM and PIM
text: PAM and PIM Privileged elevation, just-in-time access, session controls, credential custody, and zero standing privilege. A standing admin password in a vault is not the same control as a time-bound role. How does an administrator get powerful access for a short time, and what proof do we keep?

title: Shared password manager for admin credentials
text: Shared password manager for admin credentials Small admin team and no session recording requirement. Auditors ask for session evidence or just-in-time access.

title: CIEM and access intelligence
text: CIEM and access intelligence Cloud entitlement posture and the question of effective access: what a human or machine can actually do across cloud accounts. This is not automatically an IGA certification product. What can this identity really do in cloud, and which of those paths are excessive?

title: Entitlement checks inside CSPM or CNAPP
text: Entitlement checks inside CSPM or CNAPP One cloud and coarse least-privilege goals. Effective permissions across accounts and identities need to be explained and fixed.

title: Identity threat detection (ITDR)
text: Identity threat detection (ITDR) Detection, investigation, and response for identity-based attacks: token theft, directory attacks, privilege abuse, and attack paths. ITDR does not replace joiner-mover-leaver. How do we see and stop an attacker using a real identity?

title: Identity detections written in the SIEM
text: Identity detections written in the SIEM A strong detection team and clean identity logs. Identity attack paths and posture need context the SIEM doesn't hold.

title: Secrets detection and remediation
text: Secrets detection and remediation Finding credentials in code, tickets, images, chat, and other places they should not be, then verifying whether they still work and getting them rotated. Detection does not issue the replacement credential. Where are live secrets exposed, and who has to revoke them?

title: Open-source scanners in CI
text: Open-source scanners in CI A few repos, one team, and someone who owns tuning and triage. Coverage spreads past git (tickets, chat, logs, images) or nobody can tell which hits are live.

title: Secret scanning bundled in the code host or AppSec suite
text: Secret scanning bundled in the code host or AppSec suite Code lives in one host and the team only needs push protection on new commits. History, non-code sources, or verification of whether a credential still works matter.

title: Rotate after an incident
text: Rotate after an incident Small blast radius and no audit or customer pressure. A leaked credential is used, or an audit or customer asks how leaks are found.

title: Secrets management
text: Secrets management Vaulting, dynamic issuance, rotation, PKI, and key management. The secret is the credential. The workload or person using it is a separate identity. Where should this credential live, and can we issue it for a short time instead of storing it?

title: Cloud provider secret stores
text: Cloud provider secret stores One cloud, one platform team, few on-prem systems. Multi-cloud, on-prem, or dynamic credentials across many teams.

title: Environment variables and config files
text: Environment variables and config files Very early stage with a handful of services. Rotation, audit, or offboarding becomes someone's weekend.

title: NHI and workload identity
text: NHI and workload identity Service accounts, service principals, CI jobs, apps, containers, APIs, and bots. The work is discovery, ownership, purpose, lifecycle, permissions, and decommissioning. A key is not the identity. Which machine identities exist, who owns them, and which ones should already be gone?

title: Spreadsheet inventory of service accounts and keys
text: Spreadsheet inventory of service accounts and keys Dozens of machine identities with clear owners. Thousands of keys, tokens, and service accounts across SaaS and cloud, with owners who left.

title: Extend the IGA program to machine accounts
text: Extend the IGA program to machine accounts Machine accounts mostly live in the directory and follow human-like lifecycles. Most machine credentials live outside the directory (cloud roles, API keys, OAuth apps).

title: Vault plus secret scanning
text: Vault plus secret scanning The main worry is leaked or hard-coded credentials. The question becomes who owns each identity and what it can reach.

title: AI agent identity and runtime authorization
text: AI agent identity and runtime authorization Inventory of agents, human delegation, MCP or tool access, gateways, and a decision on each action. An agent that can call tools is not just another service account with a static key. Which agent is this, who authorized it, and what may it do on this call?

title: Treat agents as ordinary service accounts
text: Treat agents as ordinary service accounts A few internal agents with fixed, narrow permissions. Agents act on behalf of users, chain tools, or need per-request decisions.

title: Identity orchestration and authorization
text: Identity orchestration and authorization Policy engines and relationship-based authorization that sit beside the directory and the IGA suite. They decide an action. They are not, by themselves, a certification campaign. Where does the allow or deny happen at the moment of the call?

title: Adjacent security
text: Adjacent security CNAPP and CSPM, AppSec, DSPM and data access governance, SaaS security, and GRC. They share buyers and findings with identity. They are not automatic IGA competitors. Is this finding an identity problem, a data problem, a cloud problem, or an audit-evidence problem?

title: Security data pipeline platforms (SDPP)
text: Security data pipeline platforms (SDPP) Ingest, validate, normalize, enrich and route security telemetry before downstream SIEM, data-lake and detection systems. Pipeline health and cost controls are distinct from storage or alert investigation. Can we deliver complete, trustworthy security telemetry to the right detection and analysis destinations at an acceptable cost?

title: Filter and route inside the SIEM or its forwarders
text: Filter and route inside the SIEM or its forwarders Moderate log volume and one main destination. Ingest cost grows faster than budget, or data must go to several destinations.

title: Custom pipelines on general-purpose streaming tools
text: Custom pipelines on general-purpose streaming tools A data engineering team already runs streaming infrastructure. Security-specific parsing, enrichment, and schema changes keep breaking.

title: Detection engineering lifecycle
text: Detection engineering lifecycle Design, test, version, deploy and measure security detections using known telemetry and attack behaviors. Distinct from a SIEM analytics engine or simply triaging alerts. Can we prove our detection content fires on the right activity, remains reliable after data changes and improves investigation quality?

title: Detections written and tuned ad hoc in the SIEM console
text: Detections written and tuned ad hoc in the SIEM console A small team with a few dozen rules. Nobody can say which detections exist, what they cover, or whether they still fire.

title: Rely on vendor or MDR-provided content
text: Rely on vendor or MDR-provided content Coverage of common threats is enough and there's no detection team. Environment-specific attack paths or custom apps need detections nobody ships.

title: Endpoint security
text: Endpoint security Prevention and detection on laptops, servers, and other devices. EDR is the usual product. It is not an identity provider, even when it consumes identity signals. What runs on the device, and who responds when it is compromised?

title: Operating system built-in antivirus
text: Operating system built-in antivirus Small fleet with low risk and no EDR requirement from insurers or customers. Insurers, customers, or an incident require detection and response, not just prevention.

title: MDR provider brings its own endpoint agent
text: MDR provider brings its own endpoint agent No in-house SOC and endpoints are the main concern. The team wants to own detections, switch providers, or cover servers and cloud the same way.

title: Email security
text: Email security Inbound and outbound mail controls: phishing, impersonation, and data leaving by email. A secure email gateway and an API-based detection product are different architectures. How does a malicious or fraudulent message get stopped before someone acts on it?

title: Native filtering in the email platform
text: Native filtering in the email platform Commodity spam and malware are the main problem. Targeted phishing, business email compromise, or account takeover get through.

title: Train users to report phishing
text: Train users to report phishing Low volume of targeted attacks and a strong reporting culture. Losses from wire fraud or credential phishing happen despite training.

title: Network edge
text: Network edge Firewalls, secure web gateways, ZTNA, and SASE. Buyers collapse these into one deal. They are not one control, and they are not a substitute for workforce identity. What is allowed to connect, from where, and to which application?

title: VPN and perimeter firewalls kept as they are
text: VPN and perimeter firewalls kept as they are Mostly office-based staff and few cloud apps. Remote work, SaaS, and edge-device vulnerabilities make the perimeter the weak point.

title: Cloud provider network controls only
text: Cloud provider network controls only Workloads live in one cloud and users reach SaaS directly. User traffic, branch offices, and private apps need consistent policy.

title: IT vulnerability management
text: IT vulnerability management Missing patches and misconfigurations on IT assets: servers, endpoints, network devices. This is not software composition analysis in a repository, and it is not CSPM in a cloud account. Which of our machines are exposed, and who has to patch them?

title: Scanner output triaged by CVSS in spreadsheets
text: Scanner output triaged by CVSS in spreadsheets A small estate and a patch team with capacity. Backlogs grow faster than patching and nobody agrees what to fix first.

title: Continuous threat exposure management
text: Continuous threat exposure management A program for deciding which exposures matter, broader than traditional technology vulnerability management. It is not itself a scanner, a cloud-posture product, or a software-composition scan. Which exposures matter beyond the patch list, and who owns each one?

title: Security awareness
text: Security awareness Training and simulated phishing for people. It changes behavior. It does not replace email security or identity threat detection. Will people report the message, and is the program more than an annual video?

title: Annual compliance training video
text: Annual compliance training video Training is only needed to tick an audit box. Phishing losses or a regulator asks for measurable behavior change.

title: Static analysis (SAST)
text: Static analysis (SAST) Analysis of source or bytecode for vulnerabilities before the code runs. No capability in this atlas is checked for a SAST vendor until a current page is cited. Which defects can we see in the pull request, and who fixes them?

title: Open-source and linter-based static analysis
text: Open-source and linter-based static analysis Few languages and engineers willing to tune rules. Coverage, false positives, and reporting have to be managed at scale.

title: Dynamic testing (DAST)
text: Dynamic testing (DAST) Testing a running application from the outside. Useful against what is deployed. Blind to most source-level issues and to infrastructure posture. What can an outsider hit in staging or production, and when do we scan?

title: Periodic penetration tests instead of automated scanning
text: Periodic penetration tests instead of automated scanning Few releases a year and a compliance requirement for one test. Weekly releases outpace the test and findings arrive months late.

title: Open-source web scanners run by AppSec
text: Open-source web scanners run by AppSec A few web apps and someone to triage results. Authenticated scanning, APIs, and CI integration across many apps take too much effort.

title: Software composition analysis
text: Software composition analysis Known vulnerabilities and license risk in dependencies. This is not IT vulnerability management of servers, and it is not a secret scanner, though the same pull request can contain all three. Which libraries are we shipping, and which of those findings are reachable?

title: Dependency alerts from the code host
text: Dependency alerts from the code host One code host and basic known-vulnerability alerts are enough. Reachability, licenses, or SBOM requests from customers matter.

title: API security
text: API security Inventory and abuse of APIs the product exposes. Overlaps DAST, gateways, and runtime protection. Do not assume an API security product replaces authentication. Which APIs exist, and which of them are being called in ways we did not design?

title: API gateway auth and rate limiting
text: API gateway auth and rate limiting APIs are inventoried and all pass through one gateway. Shadow or deprecated APIs and business-logic abuse don't show up at the gateway.

title: Test APIs with existing DAST
text: Test APIs with existing DAST A small, documented API surface. APIs change faster than specs, or abuse happens in production traffic.

title: Application security posture
text: Application security posture A layer that tries to correlate SAST, SCA, secrets, and runtime findings into one backlog. It is a workflow product. It does not replace the scanners unless the contract says so. Which findings matter, and can engineering see one queue?

title: Exporting scanner findings to spreadsheets and tickets
text: Exporting scanner findings to spreadsheets and tickets Two or three scanners and one AppSec engineer. Findings from many tools need dedupe, ownership, and risk ranking.

title: One vendor's AppSec suite dashboard
text: One vendor's AppSec suite dashboard Most scanning is already from one vendor. Mixed tools, or the team wants to swap scanners without losing history.

title: Application runtime protection
text: Application runtime protection WAF, bot controls, and RASP in front of or inside a running application. This is a production shield. It is not a code fix. What stops an exploit against an application we have not patched yet?

title: CDN or cloud provider WAF rules
text: CDN or cloud provider WAF rules Public web apps with common attack patterns. Custom app logic, bots, or zero-days need deeper protection or tuning.

title: Patch fast and accept the gap
text: Patch fast and accept the gap A small app estate and a fast release process. A critical vulnerability lands in something that can't be patched quickly.

title: Product security program
text: Product security program The operating system of product security: design review, secure engineering expectations, and who signs off before a feature ships. Tools support it. The program is not a SKU. How does a feature get a security review, and what happens when the answer is no?

title: AppSec team covers product security part-time
text: AppSec team covers product security part-time One product line and few customer security demands. Customer reviews, disclosure, and secure design work outgrow the AppSec queue.

title: Engineering owns security informally
text: Engineering owns security informally Early stage with no enterprise customers yet. An enterprise deal, incident, or regulator needs a named owner and a program.

title: Threat modeling
text: Threat modeling A structured look at how a design can be abused, done before or beside the code. A workshop and a threat-modeling product are both in this category. Neither is a scan. What are we building, and how would someone abuse it?

title: Whiteboard sessions and templates in docs
text: Whiteboard sessions and templates in docs A few high-risk designs reviewed by an experienced security engineer. Design reviews become a bottleneck or happen too late to change anything.

title: Rely on testing after the code is written
text: Rely on testing after the code is written Low-risk features and a strong testing culture. Design flaws keep showing up in pentests when they're expensive to fix.

title: Disclosure and bug bounty
text: Disclosure and bug bounty How outsiders report vulnerabilities in the product, and how those reports are paid, triaged, and fixed. This is a product-security intake, not a corporate VM scanner. Where does a researcher send a report, and how fast do we fix it?

title: A security contact page and a shared inbox
text: A security contact page and a shared inbox A few reports a year from researchers. Report volume, duplicates, and payout decisions overwhelm the team.

title: Only scheduled penetration tests
text: Only scheduled penetration tests Low public exposure and no customer demand for a disclosure program. Researchers find issues anyway and have no safe way to report them.

title: Customer trust
text: Customer trust Questionnaires, penetration-test letters, and control descriptions a buyer of your product asks for. Related to GRC. The audience is the customer's security review, not your own corporate audit. Can we answer a customer's security review without inventing controls?

title: Security team answers questionnaires by hand
text: Security team answers questionnaires by hand A few enterprise deals a quarter. Questionnaires block deals and pull engineers off roadmap work.

title: Cloud posture (CSPM)
text: Cloud posture (CSPM) Misconfiguration of cloud control planes: public storage, open security groups, missing logging. Not CIEM, though the same CNAPP may sell both, and not SCA. Which cloud settings are unsafe, and who owns the account?

title: Cloud provider native posture tools
text: Cloud provider native posture tools One cloud and a team that lives in that console. Multiple clouds or prioritization across many accounts.

title: Cloud workload protection
text: Cloud workload protection Runtime protection of cloud workloads: hosts, containers, and serverless. Adjacent to endpoint security and to container security. Confirm which runtime the product actually sees. What is running in the cloud, and can we stop a bad process there?

title: Posture scanning without runtime protection
text: Posture scanning without runtime protection Workloads are short-lived and posture is the main risk. Runtime threats, crypto-mining, or container escape attempts go unseen.

title: Run the endpoint agent on cloud servers
text: Run the endpoint agent on cloud servers Long-lived VMs that look like servers. Containers, serverless, and ephemeral workloads don't fit the agent model.

title: Cloud-native application protection
text: Cloud-native application protection A suite label that bundles posture, identity entitlements, workload, and sometimes code. Treat the module on the order form as the product. Do not treat the suite name as proof of every module. Which modules are we actually licensed for?

title: Separate CSPM, workload, and IaC tools
text: Separate CSPM, workload, and IaC tools Different teams own each layer and tools are already in place. Findings need one risk view across code, cloud, and runtime.

title: Cloud detection and response
text: Cloud detection and response Detections on cloud control-plane and workload telemetry. The SOC may own the queue. Cloud security owns the log sources. This is not CSPM hygiene. How do we see an attacker using a cloud API, not just a bad setting?

title: Send cloud logs to the SIEM and write detections
text: Send cloud logs to the SIEM and write detections A strong detection team and manageable log cost. Cloud-specific attack paths need context the SIEM doesn't hold.

title: Cloud provider native threat detection
text: Cloud provider native threat detection One cloud and standard workloads. Multiple clouds or identity-based attacks need correlated detection.

title: Data security posture
text: Data security posture Discovery and classification of sensitive data in the stores a product can see, and the paths that can reach it. A posture finding is not a block on the way out. It is not an identity certification, and a CNAPP data module is a module until the order form says otherwise. Where is the sensitive data, and which identities can reach it?

title: Data inventory by survey and data owners
text: Data inventory by survey and data owners Few data stores and a privacy program with engaged owners. Shadow data stores, AI training data, or an audit asks where sensitive data lives.

title: Data loss prevention
text: Data loss prevention Controls on data leaving through email, the endpoint, the web, or SaaS. Those are different enforcement points. A DSPM scan of a bucket does not stop a download. Logging an event is not the same as blocking it. A key in a chat message can also be a secrets-detection finding. Where can sensitive data leave, and what do we block versus log?

title: DLP features in the email or endpoint suite
text: DLP features in the email or endpoint suite Most exfiltration risk is email and laptops. SaaS, AI tools, and code repos become the main leak paths.

title: Privacy governance
text: Privacy governance Records of processing, consent, data-subject requests, and privacy reviews. Legal and privacy own it. Security supplies the technical controls. Do not sell a scanner as a privacy program. Can we say what personal data we hold and why?

title: Records of processing and DSARs tracked in spreadsheets
text: Records of processing and DSARs tracked in spreadsheets Low request volume and one main regulation. Requests, data maps, and regulations multiply across regions.

title: Outside counsel runs privacy compliance
text: Outside counsel runs privacy compliance Few systems and infrequent changes. Product changes outpace reviews and costs climb.

title: Data access governance
text: Data access governance Policy on who may query or read a dataset, usually at a catalog, warehouse, or database. Identity governance reviews the account. This reviews the data grant. A DSPM path is not enforcement in the query. Who can query this data, and is that grant still appropriate?

title: Data owners review access in tickets
text: Data owners review access in tickets A few sensitive data stores with clear owners. Access sprawls across SaaS, warehouses, and AI tools.

title: Extend IGA certifications to data stores
text: Extend IGA certifications to data stores Data access mostly follows application roles. Fine-grained permissions in warehouses and file shares don't map to app roles.

title: Database security
text: Database security Activity monitoring and controls on the database itself. It watches queries. It is not a cloud posture scan and not file-share DLP. Which queries ran, and can a bad one be stopped at the database?

title: Native database audit logs and access controls
text: Native database audit logs and access controls Few databases with a capable DBA team. Many engines, cloud databases, and audit requirements make native tools inconsistent.

title: Use data posture discovery for database risk
text: Use data posture discovery for database risk The main question is where sensitive data lives. Activity monitoring and blocking privileged misuse are required.

title: Encryption and tokenization
text: Encryption and tokenization Encryption, tokenization, or key control for the data itself. A key manager is not a discovery product. A secrets vault stores the credential. This category is about protecting the data that credential can reach. No algorithm is checked here. Is the data protected when the store or the file is copied, and who holds the keys?

title: Cloud provider encryption at rest and key management
text: Cloud provider encryption at rest and key management Data stays in one cloud and default encryption meets requirements. Field-level protection, tokenization for compliance scope, or customer-held keys are needed.

title: Application teams encrypt fields themselves
text: Application teams encrypt fields themselves One or two apps with a careful team. Key rotation, consistency, and audit across many apps fall apart.

title: SIEM
text: SIEM The place logs are collected, detections are written, and investigations start. Identity, endpoint, and cloud products may send signals here. The SIEM does not grant access. Which logs do we have, and can an analyst ask a question in time?

title: Logs in a data lake with in-house detections
text: Logs in a data lake with in-house detections A strong data engineering team and cost pressure on ingest. Detection content, case management, and analyst workflow have to be built and maintained.

title: Let the MDR provider own detection
text: Let the MDR provider own detection No in-house SOC and endpoint coverage is the main need. Custom detections, cloud and identity coverage, or log retention requirements grow.

title: SOAR and response automation
text: SOAR and response automation Playbooks that enrich and sometimes contain an incident. Automation that disables a user is powerful and dangerous. It is not joiner-mover-leaver. Which response steps are safe to automate, and who approves the rest?

title: Scripts and workflow automation tools
text: Scripts and workflow automation tools A few repeatable playbooks and an engineer who owns them. Many playbooks, approvals, and audit of automated actions.

title: Control evidence and risk
text: Control evidence and risk The risk register, control tests, and audit evidence. GRC platforms track whether a control operated. The control itself lives in identity, AppSec, cloud, or IT. Which controls do we claim, and where is the evidence from the last period?

title: Spreadsheets, screenshots, and shared drives for audit evidence
text: Spreadsheets, screenshots, and shared drives for audit evidence One framework and a single audit a year. Multiple frameworks, continuous monitoring, or audit prep eats the team for weeks.

title: Third-party risk
text: Third-party risk Assessments of vendors and subprocessors. Related to customer trust when you are the vendor being assessed. The questionnaire is not a technical test of their product. Which suppliers can affect us, and what did we actually review?

title: Questionnaires by email
text: Questionnaires by email A short vendor list reviewed once a year. Hundreds of vendors, continuous monitoring, or a third-party breach.

title: Breach and attack simulation
text: Breach and attack simulation Platforms that safely run attacker techniques to see whether controls detect or block them. A control that was never tested is a claim. This category tests the claim. No vendor here has a capability checkmark yet. Which techniques do our controls actually see?

title: Annual pentest or red team engagement
text: Annual pentest or red team engagement Controls change slowly and one test a year satisfies stakeholders. Teams need to know whether controls still work after every change.

title: Open-source attack simulation frameworks
text: Open-source attack simulation frameworks A detection engineer has time to run and maintain tests. Coverage, reporting, and safe scheduling across the estate become too much work.

title: Penetration testing
text: Penetration testing Human testing of a scoped target, plus the program that commissions and tracks it. A letter for customers is customer trust. The findings belong to the team that owns the system. What was in scope, who tested it, and which findings are still open?

title: Annual third-party penetration test
text: Annual third-party penetration test Compliance needs one report a year. Release frequency outpaces the test, or customers ask for continuous coverage.

title: Container and Kubernetes security
text: Container and Kubernetes security Images, admission, runtime, and cluster configuration. Overlaps SCA for image contents, CWPP for runtime, and secrets management when the cluster needs a credential. What is in the image, what is allowed to run, and how does the workload authenticate?

title: Open-source image scanners and admission policies
text: Open-source image scanners and admission policies A few clusters and a platform team that owns policy. Many clusters, runtime threats, and reporting across teams.

title: Container coverage inside a CNAPP
text: Container coverage inside a CNAPP Kubernetes is one part of a broader cloud estate. Deep Kubernetes runtime or policy needs exceed the suite.

title: Infrastructure-as-code security
text: Infrastructure-as-code security Review of Terraform, CloudFormation, and similar before apply. It catches the change in the pull request. CSPM catches what is already deployed. Both can be true. Can we stop a bad cloud change before it is applied?

title: Open-source IaC linters in CI
text: Open-source IaC linters in CI A few repos and engineers who fix findings. Rules, exceptions, and drift between code and cloud need managing at scale.

title: Catch misconfigurations after deploy with CSPM
text: Catch misconfigurations after deploy with CSPM Infrastructure changes are infrequent. Fixing in production is slower and riskier than catching it in the pull request.

title: Extended detection and response
text: Extended detection and response Detection and response sold together across more than the endpoint. This map does not treat that name as a SIEM replacement, and it does not treat it as an identity provider. Which signals are correlated, and who is allowed to contain a host or an account?

title: Keep EDR and SIEM separate
text: Keep EDR and SIEM separate Established SIEM and detection team. Analysts drown in context switching and correlation across tools.

title: Buy outcomes from an MDR instead
text: Buy outcomes from an MDR instead No SOC and no plan to build one. The team wants control of detections and data.

title: Managed detection and response
text: Managed detection and response A provider watches alerts and responds under a contract. The technology may be theirs or the customer's. MDR is an operating model. It is not proof that a particular detection exists. Who is on the hook after hours, and which actions may they take without us?

title: Build an in-house 24x7 SOC
text: Build an in-house 24x7 SOC Large enterprise with budget for shifts and retention. Hiring, burnout, or coverage gaps on nights and weekends.

title: Network detection and response
text: Network detection and response Detection from network traffic and metadata. This map keeps it as its own category beside endpoint detection. A firewall log in a SIEM is not the same purchase. What can we see on the wire that the endpoint agent will miss?

title: Open-source network IDS and flow logs
text: Open-source network IDS and flow logs A small network and a skilled analyst. Encrypted traffic, east-west visibility, and alert volume outgrow it.

title: Rely on endpoint and identity telemetry
text: Rely on endpoint and identity telemetry Most assets run an endpoint agent. Unmanaged devices, OT, or lateral movement hide where agents don't run.

title: Threat intelligence
text: Threat intelligence Finished reporting and indicator feeds that detection teams use. This map keeps the feed as its own category. A feed is not a detection, and a report is not an incident response retainer unless the contract says so. Which actors and indicators does this team need, and who turns them into detections?

title: Free feeds and community sharing groups
text: Free feeds and community sharing groups Basic indicator blocking and a small team. Analysts need context, relevance, and fewer false positives.

title: Intelligence bundled in the EDR or SIEM
text: Intelligence bundled in the EDR or SIEM Intelligence is consumed only inside detections. Strategic reporting, takedowns, or sector-specific intelligence are required.

title: File and malware analysis
text: File and malware analysis Deciding whether a file is malicious, what it was built to do, and what it is related to, using static analysis, sandbox detonation, signatures, reputation or code similarity. Some products also keep the customer's own files and re-check them as intelligence changes. A verdict on a file is not proof of where it spread, and a public lookup service is not a private repository. Is this file malicious, what else looks like it, and has it been in our environment before?

title: Free public lookup and sandbox services
text: Free public lookup and sandbox services Occasional files that are not sensitive. Internal binaries cannot be uploaded publicly, or the team needs to know where else the file has been.

title: File verdicts built into the EDR or XDR
text: File verdicts built into the EDR or XDR The EDR verdict is enough to close the alert. Analysts need related variants, history across hosts, or an explained verdict.

title: SaaS security posture
text: SaaS security posture Posture of sanctioned SaaS: configuration, third-party apps, and OAuth grants. Shortlists also print CASB in this box. A gateway that proxies traffic is not the same product as a configuration check. It overlaps non-human identity when the question is which app holds a token. It does not replace IGA. Which SaaS apps are connected, and which grants should not still be standing?

title: Periodic manual reviews of SaaS admin settings
text: Periodic manual reviews of SaaS admin settings A few critical SaaS apps with known admins. Dozens of apps, third-party integrations, and drift between reviews.

title: Rely on CASB or SSE visibility
text: Rely on CASB or SSE visibility Main concern is user traffic to SaaS. Misconfigured SaaS settings and OAuth integrations aren't visible in traffic.

title: Web application and API protection
text: Web application and API protection Inline controls in front of a web application and its APIs, including blocking and bot checks. This map keeps that edge separate from static analysis, and separate from an API inventory unless that module is licensed. What sits in front of the application, and what does it block?

title: CDN-included WAF rules
text: CDN-included WAF rules Standard web apps and default rule sets. APIs, bots, and custom rules need dedicated tuning.

title: Rely on secure code and patching
text: Rely on secure code and patching Internal or low-traffic apps. A public app faces bots, credential stuffing, or an unpatched flaw.

title: Microsegmentation
text: Microsegmentation Workload-to-workload policy, usually sold apart from the perimeter firewall. This map keeps it as its own category. It does not decide which human may sign in. Which workloads may talk, and how is that policy enforced after the firewall?

title: VLANs and firewall rules
text: VLANs and firewall rules A simple network with few east-west flows. Ransomware lateral movement or audit scope reduction needs workload-level policy.

title: Cloud security groups only
text: Cloud security groups only Workloads are all in one cloud. Hybrid estates need consistent policy across data center and cloud.

title: External attack surface
text: External attack surface Discovery of internet-facing assets and the exposures on them. This map keeps that search separate from a missing-patch scan on a known server, and separate from a search for abuse of a brand the organization already knows. What is exposed that our asset list does not mention?

title: Periodic scans with open-source tools
text: Periodic scans with open-source tools A known, small set of domains and IPs. Acquisitions, shadow IT, and cloud sprawl make the surface unknown.

title: Digital risk protection
text: Digital risk protection A search for public abuse of a brand, domain, executive, product, or customer-facing asset the organization already knows. That search is not an inventory of unknown internet-facing hosts, and it is not a missing-patch scan. Which public abuse of a known brand is in scope, and who owns the asset being abused?

title: Cyber asset management
text: Cyber asset management A consolidated inventory of devices, accounts, and cloud assets from the tools that already see them. This map uses cyber asset attack surface management for that inventory. It is the list. It is not the scanner and not the EDR. Can we name every asset, and which tool is the source of truth?

title: CMDB plus spreadsheets
text: CMDB plus spreadsheets A stable estate and a disciplined IT team. Cloud, SaaS, and shadow IT make the CMDB wrong within weeks.

title: Inventory views in existing EDR and cloud consoles
text: Inventory views in existing EDR and cloud consoles Most assets are covered by one or two tools. Nobody can answer what exists across all tools, or what's unmanaged.

title: OT and IoT security
text: OT and IoT security Visibility and detection for operational technology and unmanaged devices. This map keeps that work apart from corporate endpoint detection, because many of these assets cannot run an endpoint agent. What is on the plant or device network, and what is it talking to?

title: Air gaps and network segmentation
text: Air gaps and network segmentation Isolated plants with little remote access. Remote access, IT/OT convergence, or a regulator needs visibility into OT traffic.

title: Extend IT security tools into OT
text: Extend IT security tools into OT A few OT assets that behave like IT systems. Industrial protocols and fragile devices can't take IT agents or scans.

title: Insider risk
text: Insider risk Behavior that suggests data theft or misuse by someone who already has access. This map keeps that investigation separate from a data-loss block and from identity threat detection. Which departing or misusing user is moving data, and who is allowed to look?

title: DLP rules plus HR investigations
text: DLP rules plus HR investigations Clear data types and infrequent cases. Context on user behavior is needed to separate mistakes from intent.

title: Handle cases as they come up
text: Handle cases as they come up Low-value data and few departures. A departing employee takes customer data or source code.

title: Security ratings
text: Security ratings Outside-in scores of a company's exposed posture, used in third-party risk and insurance conversations. This map keeps a score separate from an assessment the supplier filled out, and separate from a penetration test. Whose outside-in score are we using, and what decision does it actually change?

title: Questionnaires and SOC 2 reports only
text: Questionnaires and SOC 2 reports only A short vendor list reviewed yearly. Continuous monitoring or board reporting on third-party risk is required.

title: No outside-in scoring
text: No outside-in scoring Customers and insurers don't ask. An insurer, board, or customer starts quoting a rating at you.

title: Enterprise browser
text: Enterprise browser A managed browser as the work surface, used alongside virtual desktop and secure web gateway controls. This map keeps the browser as its own category. It still depends on workforce identity. Is the control the browser, the network path, or the identity that opens the app?

title: Managed standard browser with policies and extensions
text: Managed standard browser with policies and extensions Basic controls on managed devices are enough. Contractors, unmanaged devices, or data controls inside SaaS are required.

title: VDI or remote desktop for risky access
text: VDI or remote desktop for risky access A few high-risk user groups. VDI cost and user experience don't scale to everyone.

title: AI application security
text: AI application security Controls aimed at models and AI features, including prompt injection and model abuse. Securing the model remains a different job from deciding which tools an agent may call. Is the issue the model, the application around it, or the identity the agent uses?

title: Manual red teaming and prompt reviews before launch
text: Manual red teaming and prompt reviews before launch A few AI features with low exposure. Many AI features ship continuously and prompts change weekly.

title: Model provider safety filters
text: Model provider safety filters Low-risk use cases with no sensitive data. Prompt injection, data leakage, or tool misuse matters for the business.

title: Runtime-validated application security
text: Runtime-validated application security Application security checks meant to be judged against the running system, not only against a static finding. A finding whose exploitability is unknown is still a finding. Was this finding checked against the running system, or only against the source?

title: Cyber recovery
text: Cyber recovery Backup and recovery built for a ransomware event: immutable copies and a tested restore. This map keeps that restore separate from a GRC evidence collection. A backup product does not collect audit evidence, and a GRC platform does not restore a domain. What can we restore, from when, and has anyone tested that restore?

title: Standard backups with retention policies
text: Standard backups with retention policies Backups are tested and isolated from production credentials. Ransomware targets backups, or recovery has never been tested end to end.

title: Rely on cyber insurance and incident response retainers
text: Rely on cyber insurance and incident response retainers Low dependence on systems for revenue. Insurers require tested recovery, or downtime costs exceed coverage.

title: Agentic runtime enforcement
text: Agentic runtime enforcement A check on a live agent action before it completes. Directory, governance, privileged access, and non-human inventory remain necessary and do not decide whether that action should continue. This map does not score the control. Can anything stop or narrow an agent action while it is still running?

title: Agent permissions set by hand in each tool
text: Agent permissions set by hand in each tool A few internal agents with narrow scopes. Agents act for many users and need per-request decisions and logging.

title: Allow agents and review logs afterward
text: Allow agents and review logs afterward Pilots with no sensitive data. An agent takes a harmful action that nobody could have stopped in time.

title: Endpoint control and prevention
text: Endpoint control and prevention Controls aimed at what a device is doing above the file and the process: developer tools, SaaS, AI tools, and local agents. Endpoint detection remains the process and file record. This map does not treat the broader layer as a replacement for that record. What is happening above the operating system, and can the device stop it?

title: Group policy and MDM restrictions
text: Group policy and MDM restrictions Standard devices and a small set of approved apps. Developers, admin rights, and new tools make static rules break or get bypassed.

title: Detect with EDR instead of preventing
text: Detect with EDR instead of preventing The team prefers alerting over blocking. Prevention is required for unapproved software, AI tools, or ransomware.

title: MCP and tool security
text: MCP and tool security Discovery and control of Model Context Protocol servers and the tools an agent can call. A gateway can enforce on traffic it sees and does not see why the agent acted. Direct access can see more of the behavior and does not by itself enforce the policy. Neither pattern is a sourced product capability here. Which tool servers exist, and can an unapproved tool answer the agent?

title: An approved list of MCP servers and tools
text: An approved list of MCP servers and tools A few developers trying MCP. MCP spreads across teams and tools call internal systems.

title: Treat MCP like any other developer tool
text: Treat MCP like any other developer tool Experiments only, with no production access. MCP servers get credentials to real systems.

title: AI data security
text: AI data security Sensitive data entering a prompt, retrieved by an agent, or leaving through a tool. This is data context for an AI workflow. It is not the same control as DSPM for data stores, and it is not agent identity. Which sensitive data can this workflow see, and where can that data go?

title: Extend DLP to AI tools
text: Extend DLP to AI tools Main concern is users pasting data into chat tools. Training data, retrieval pipelines, and model outputs need protection too.

title: An AI use policy and approved tools list
text: An AI use policy and approved tools list Few AI tools in use. Shadow AI use grows faster than the policy is enforced.

title: Model and infrastructure security
text: Model and infrastructure security The model supply chain, how a model is deployed, and protection of the runtime that serves it. Distinct from testing prompts in an application and from deciding which tools an agent may call. Which model is running, where, and what can reach that runtime?

title: Cloud AI platform security defaults
text: Cloud AI platform security defaults Models run on one managed AI platform. Self-hosted models, model supply chain, or GPU infrastructure need their own controls.

title: Cover AI infrastructure with existing cloud posture tools
text: Cover AI infrastructure with existing cloud posture tools AI workloads look like other cloud workloads. Model artifacts, training pipelines, and model files need AI-specific checks.

title: AI governance
text: AI governance Inventory of AI systems, the policy that applies to them, and the audit trail. Governance records the decision. It does not, by itself, stop a tool call or scan a prompt. Which AI systems are approved, who owns them, and where is the record?

title: An acceptable-use policy and a review committee
text: An acceptable-use policy and a review committee Few AI tools and low regulatory exposure. Teams adopt AI tools faster than reviews run, or regulation requires inventories.

title: Software supply chain
text: Software supply chain The path from a dependency, image, or build to what runs in production. SCA, SBOM, and secrets detection are pieces of it. A supply-chain product is not a SAST scanner and not a vault unless the quote says so. What went into the build, and can we say where a package came from?

title: Generate SBOMs on request
text: Generate SBOMs on request Few customers ask and releases are infrequent. Customers or regulators expect continuous attestations and build integrity.

title: Cloud vulnerability management
text: Cloud vulnerability management Scanning and assessment of cloud workloads and images. Buyers mix this with corporate vulnerability management and with CSPM. A missing package on a cloud host is not the same finding as a public storage bucket. Which cloud workloads are being assessed, and who patches them?

title: Run traditional vulnerability scanners on cloud hosts
text: Run traditional vulnerability scanners on cloud hosts Long-lived VMs that behave like on-prem servers. Containers, images, and ephemeral workloads need agentless or image scanning.

title: Cloud provider native vulnerability scanning
text: Cloud provider native vulnerability scanning One cloud and simple workloads. Prioritization across clouds and accounts becomes the problem.

title: Interactive application testing
text: Interactive application testing Testing from inside a running application, often with an agent in test. Buyers put it next to SAST and DAST. It is not a production runtime firewall. Is the sensor in a test run, or is it trying to block production traffic?

title: Keep SAST and DAST without instrumentation
text: Keep SAST and DAST without instrumentation Teams resist agents in test environments. False positives and missing runtime context slow triage.

title: Rely on code review and pentests
text: Rely on code review and pentests Few apps and slow release cycles. Release frequency and app count outgrow manual review.
